name: Good Goods: A Novel of the Distribution Years
creator: Reuben Castellanos-Park
description: A sweeping, Axiom-approved literary novel following three generations of a family employed by a corponation logistics division from 2155 to 2210, told through their relationships with the goods they move — food, chrome, geneware, weapons — and what those goods mean at each tier of Meridian society. The prose is precise and emotionally restrained, praised for its 'authentic working-class voice' by Tier 4 literary critics. It won the Meridian Compact Fiction Prize in 2221 and has sold over two million neural-feed downloads.
cultural_impact: Became a cultural touchstone for Tier 3 readers who saw their lives reflected in fiction for the first time in years, though debate persists about whether the novel's ultimately hopeful ending constitutes honest representation or corporate myth-making. The Meridian Compact Fiction Prize is funded by Axiom, a fact that colors all discussion of the book.
controversy: Shelf-based critics and zine writers have been scathing, arguing the novel's working-class characters never meaningfully resist their conditions and that the 'authentic voice' Castellanos-Park employs is a Tier 4 academic's approximation of how poor people speak. Castellanos-Park, who grew up in Tier 2, has responded with evident pain to these critiques.
story_hooks: An early draft of the novel, obtained through a source at Castellanos-Park's publisher, contains a fourth storyline that was cut — one following a logistics worker who helps route stolen medical chrome to the Shelf. Someone wants that draft published.
The real family whose story inspired the novel has never been credited and is living in Tier 1; one of them has started showing up at Castellanos-Park's public readings.
A Shelf pirate press has released an unauthorized 'corrected edition' with the ending rewritten, and it's becoming more widely read on the Shelf than the original.
